evidence.quote: The superior combination of the strength-ductility for the Cantor alloy at 77 K is attributed to the deformation twinning.

mechanisms.name: grain boundary relaxation
mechanisms.material_state: UFG after annealing at 923 K for 30 min

evidence.quote: The UFG alloy exhibited plastic instability and was prominently strengthened with increasing testing temperature from 293 K to 473 K, which was related to obviously grain boundaries relaxation in HEAs.

mechanisms.name: dynamic Hall-Petch effect
mechanisms.material_state: UFG after annealing at 923 K for 30 min

evidence.quote: newly formed twin boundaries firstly act as a coherent and stable interface strongly obstructing the dislocation movement, secondly cause continuous grain fragmentation, which reduces the mean free path of dislocation glide and causes dynamic Hall-Petch effect

However, our results in Fig. 8 reveal that the grain boundary relaxation of UFG Cantor is activated when the temperature increases from 293 K to 473 K. The grain boundary relaxation reduces the defect density within grain boundaries, which inhibits the dislocation climb during deformation.

In addition, it was also proposed that the plastic strain of UFG materials can be facilitated by dislocation climb, which requires sufficient spatial position within grain boundary to accommodate dislocation climb [41,42].
The critical twinning stress of UFG Cantor alloy decreases at 77 K, which attributes to the decrease of stacking fault energy with the temperature.
